verdict.rationale: MotherDuck documents a way to restrict an AI assistant to read-only access through its MCP server, and it can grant read access to specific users or roles. Together these are a first-party least-privilege control for agents. The docs do not say this is done by issuing a scoped API credential or token to the agent, so only the core idea of limiting agent privileges is evidenced. Missing for 10: explicit issuance of scoped or least-privilege API tokens for agents, granular permission scopes on credentials, token lifecycle (expiry/revocation), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent
